records.contract: f(out: *mut std::string) -> *mut std::string; writes the constant 20-byte string "Not supported on x86" into *out and returns out; the only input is the out-pointer, there is no data-dependent branch and no CPUID or feature check anywhere in the body
records.identity: rocksdb::crc32c::IsFastCrc32Supported(), returning std::string; librocksdb-sys 0.11.0+8.1.1: _ZN7rocksdb6crc32c20IsFastCrc32SupportedB5cxx11Ev, per vendor-census record node115-vendor-61c2400 whose target_body_sha256 matches the bytes hashed from the node binary. The B5cxx11 ABI tag in the mangled name marks a std::__cxx11::basic_string return: a g++ mangling check shows std::string rocksdb::crc32c::IsFastCrc32Supported() mangles to exactly this name, while a bool-returning sibling mangles without the tag. The constant "Not supported on x86" body is the not-supported branch (no CPUID or feature check in the body, consistent with a build without the SSE4.2 fast-CRC path; inference).
records.semantics: endbr64; out (*rdi, saved in %rbx) is initialised as an empty SSO string; a stack string A is built as _M_replace(0, 0, "x86", 3) from the .rodata literal at 0x441cd7; a stack string C reserves A.len + 17 = 20, appends "Not supported on " (17 bytes, .rodata 0x442afe) then appends A (3 bytes), so C = "Not supported on x86"; out appends C (20 bytes) under the std::string max_size guard; heap buffers are disposed (C is heap-allocated at 20 bytes, A stays SSO at 3 bytes); returns the out-pointer in %rax

records.observation: the vendor-census record node115-vendor-61c2400 labels this address librocksdb-sys 0.11.0+8.1.1: _ZN7rocksdb6crc32c20IsFastCrc32SupportedB5cxx11Ev with target_body_sha256 5e8cffdcbf4b8f146fbc9ea17cd45b15a700af7fce2c54fa6904d35e101bcb6f, and that hash DOES match the bytes hashed from the node binary. The label is CONFIRMED, not wrong: the B5cxx11 ABI tag in the mangled name marks a std::__cxx11::basic_string return (a g++ mangling check shows std::string rocksdb::crc32c::IsFastCrc32Supported() mangles to exactly this name, while a bool-returning sibling mangles without the tag), and the body does return a std::string — the constant "Not supported on x86". An earlier draft of this packet claimed the label was wrong on the assumption that IsFastCrc32Supported returns bool; that assumption is refuted by the mangled name itself (slopbot limited review on revision 98528507f, corrected in-PR the same cycle). The companion cold record node115-vendor-61c23b9 (label ...IsFastCrc32SupportedB5cxx11Ev.cold, target_body_sha256 6c1d7659ad52a2360fe662271467420fd7b134452321279fd43ba5e90a234345) is likewise confirmed: its hash matches the bytes hashed from the node binary, so the cold block belongs to this function.
the .rodata literal at 0x441cd7 is "x86" (3 bytes plus NUL); the lea at 0x61c2412 loads it into %rcx and _M_replace(0, 0, rcx, 3) at 0x61c2469 makes stack string A exactly those 3 bytes
the .rodata literal at 0x442afe is "Not supported on " (17 bytes plus NUL); _M_append(0x442afe, 0x11) at 0x61c24cf appends all 17 bytes to stack string C

the .rodata literal at 0x4474d2 is "basic_string::append" (21 bytes plus NUL); all three length-error paths (0x61c2583, 0x61c25a4, 0x61c25c0) pass it to __throw_length_error at 0x63f0de0, the standard libstdc++ throw argument for std::string::append

the 63-byte cold block at 0x61c23b9..0x61c23f8 is this function's exception cleanup: three staggered landing-pad entries (see landing_pad records) dispose the live strings with std::string::_M_dispose via the PLT stub at 0x63f0db0, check the stack canary at 0x58(%rsp), and rethrow the saved exception object (%r12) with _Unwind_Resume at 0x63f0a50; a canary mismatch calls __stack_chk_fail at 0x63f0d70. Every instruction in the block is reachable: 0x61c23b9 is the full-cleanup entry, 0x61c23c1 the partial entry, and 0x61c23e9 the entry that disposes C before joining the partial entry; _Unwind_Resume never returns, so control never falls through from it to 0x61c23e9, but that address is reached by jump from the landing pad at 0x61c25d8. (An earlier draft called this code "unreachable filler"; that was wrong — slopbot limited review on revision 0c98e5894, corrected in-PR the same cycle.) Census record node115-vendor-61c23b9 labels it ...IsFastCrc32SupportedB5cxx11Ev.cold; the label is confirmed with the function (see census_confirmation record).
endbr64; mov %rax,%r12 (save the exception object); jmp 0x61c23b9 — the full cleanup entry: dispose C, A and out, then canary check and _Unwind_Resume
endbr64; mov %rax,%r12 (save the exception object); jmp 0x61c23e9 — enters the cold block at 0x61c23e9: dispose C, then jmp 0x61c23c1 to dispose A and out, then canary check and _Unwind_Resume
endbr64; mov %rax,%r12 (save the exception object); jmp 0x61c23c1 — the partial cleanup entry: dispose A and out only (C not yet constructed at this call site), then canary check and _Unwind_Resume

each of the three appends is guarded by the std::string max_size check (max_size 0x3fffffffffffffff minus the current length, compared against the appended length: 17 at 0x61c24b6 with jbe to 0x61c2573, A.len at 0x61c24e3 with jb to 0x61c25b0, C.len at 0x61c2514 with jb to 0x61c2594); a failed guard checks the stack canary and calls __throw_length_error("basic_string::append") at 0x63f0de0. With the constant lengths here (17, 3, 20) the guards can never fire.

after the appends, C is disposed with the std::string::_M_dispose shape: its _M_p at [rsp+0x30] is compared with its SSO buffer at rsp+0x40; they differ (C holds 20 bytes, past the 15-byte SSO limit, so it is heap-allocated) and the heap buffer is freed with operator delete(_M_p, _M_capacity + 1) via _ZdlPvm at 0x63f0d80. A is disposed the same way at 0x61c2539: its _M_p at [rsp+0x10] equals its SSO buffer at rsp+0x20 (A holds 3 bytes), so no delete runs.

records.observation: exactly ONE direct call site in the whole .text: 0x5d87363, inside rocksdb::DBImpl::DBImpl(const DBOptions&, const std::string&) (census node115-vendor-5d85480, FDE 0x5d85480..0x5d878e2). No lea instruction anywhere in .text takes the address 0x61c2400, so there is no function-pointer or vtable use; no direct call targets the cold entry 0x61c23b9.
